deterministic_replay_guard.note: The one-off diagnostics intentionally stopped before mechanism aggregation because replayed final records did not exactly match the Worker #2 receipt.

native_play_game_probe.conclusion: Mismatch is present in the uninstrumented original play_game/policy path, not introduced by the diagnostic wrapper.

first_divergence.explanation: The same tied best-move set was present, but two candidate origins swapped order across PYTHONHASHSEED values, so seeded rng.choice selected a different placement.

determinism_diagnosis.root_cause: legal_moves iterated board.candidate_origins(rotated) as an unordered set. candidate-origin insertion/iteration order could vary across Python hash seeds because upstream tunnel-edge frozenset traversal affects insertion order. Equal-scoring candidate order therefore changed across processes, making seeded tie-breaking process-dependent.

correctness_fix.change: Canonicalize candidate origins with sorted(board.candidate_origins(rotated)) before constructing legal Move order.

mechanism_diagnosis.reason: The orchestrator required exact reproduction of all 800 Worker #2 final records before turn-level interpretation. That prerequisite failed. The historical 16 V4-only / 6 WaterSpaceV3-only groups cannot be reconstructed reliably after canonicalizing tie order, so answering the requested mechanism questions from new trajectories would mix different seed mappings.

worker_2_evidence_status.note: Worker #2's run remains a historical record, but its per-seed trajectories and discordant seed grouping are not reproducible under the project's seeded-simulation contract. The mother/orchestrator should decide how to treat its confirmatory classification after this correctness finding.

recommended_next_hypothesis: After deterministic tie ordering is fixed, replaying the already-spent seeds 2000-2399 will establish a canonical non-confirmatory baseline from which the compactness versus EXIT/no-legal-move mechanism can be diagnosed without consuming fresh seeds.
